title: Hard-delete endpoint (`DELETE /:evidenceId/hard`) has no retention period check, no immutability lock on approved/submitted evidence — two clicks permanently destroys certification evidence; violates A.5.33
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.controller.js:436-500` (`hardDeleteEvidence` handler)
**Root Cause (original):** The `DELETE /:evidenceId/hard` route blocked hard-delete unless `evidence.status === 'archived'`, but a repo-wide search for `retentionPeriod`, `RETENTION_PERIOD`, `isImmutable`, and `immutab` across the entire evidence module returned zero matches — no time-based retention enforcement and no immutability lock of any kind.
**Impact (original):** Direct violation of ISO 27001:2022 A.5.33. Evidence could be archived-then-immediately-hard-deleted with no retention window.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend` (`feature/dev`, commit 8641818). `hardDeleteEvidence` (lines 440-527) now has three sequential gates: (1) the pre-existing archived-only status gate; (2) a real retention-period lock (lines 472-495) — `RETENTION_PERIOD_DAYS` env var (default 2555/~7yr), computed against `evidence.archivedAt`, rejecting with a 400 naming the exact eligible-on date; (3) a real immutability lock (lines 497-516) — checks `WorkflowEntry.exists({entityType:'evidence', entityId, status:'closed'})` and permanently blocks hard-delete of any evidence that was ever formally approved, even past its retention window. Every attempt (blocked or successful) is logged to the audit trail with actor/timestamp/reason, closing fix-prompt item 3 as well. **Residual gap (Low, not blocking):** the retention check is `if (evidence.archivedAt) {...}` — legacy evidence archived before this field existed (`archivedAt: null`) would skip the retention check silently. Worth a follow-up backfill migration, but the core Critical control (retention + immutability) is genuinely in place for all evidence archived going forward.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.controller.js:472-516` — retention-period lock (`RETENTION_PERIOD_DAYS`, default 2555 days, computed from `evidence.archivedAt`) and immutability lock (`WorkflowEntry.exists({entityType:'evidence', status:'closed'})`) both confirmed present and logically correct on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` (commit 8641818, fast-forwarded from 9bc7ed00). No regression found in the surrounding hard-delete flow (cascade soft-delete of linked Patch/Vuln/SBOM reports and audit logging both still intact).

title: Review decision comment has no minimum length — blank or single-character approval accepted in `EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx`; certification body would challenge approvals with no justification; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx:595-644`; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflowTransition.service.js:99-100`; `vibrantix-backend/src/core/constants/featureWorkflows.js:92`
**Root Cause (original):** Frontend only required the comment be non-empty after `.trim()`. Backend `workflowTransition.service.js:99` also only checked truthiness, and `featureWorkflows.js:92`'s `commentRequiredTransitions` meant the backend required a comment ONLY for Reject — Approve had no backend comment requirement whatsoever.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend`/`vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`). Frontend `EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx` now gates Approve/Reject/Start Review on a real `MIN_COMMENT_LENGTH` constant with inline helper text showing `({comment.trim().length}/{MIN_COMMENT_LENGTH})`. Backend `workflowTransition.service.js:96-104` now requires `opts.comment.trim().length >= 50` (not just truthy) whenever `transitionDef.commentRequired` is set. `featureWorkflows.js:91` now reads `commentRequiredTransitions: [['under_review', 'needs_revision'], ['under_review', 'closed']]` — Approve is now server-side gated too, closing the asymmetry with Reject. No regression found: the same transition service change also added `submittedAt`/`reviewedAt` anchor timestamps on the `evidence` entity type as a side benefit for EM-025's review-duration metric.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflowTransition.service.js:96-104` (50-char min length enforced) + `src/core/constants/featureWorkflows.js:91` (`commentRequiredTransitions` now covers both reject and approve) + `vibrantix-client-panel/.../EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx` (`MIN_COMMENT_LENGTH` gate on all three action buttons) — all confirmed present on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` on both repos (backend fast-forwarded 9bc7ed00→8641818, client-panel fast-forwarded 9a5bac4f→d400be5a).

title: Export/Share feature is a UI mockup — 'Generate Secure Link', 'Send via Email', 'Portal Access' cards have no click handlers or functional modals in `ExportShareContent.jsx`; presented as fully implemented; violates Clause 7.5.3
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27 in `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/ExportShareContent.jsx`: all three cards now have real onClick handlers via `handleShareAction` (lines 220-285). Secure Link calls `POST /evidence/share/secure-link` (line 223) and copies the returned link to clipboard; Email Share opens a real modal (lines 641-671) and calls `POST /evidence/share/email` (line 305) via `submitEmailShare`; Portal Access calls `POST /evidence/share/portal-access` (line 246) and opens the returned URL. Each has a graceful fallback (local link / mailto: / direct navigation) if its backend call fails, rather than doing nothing. The `staticRecentExports` hardcoded array is gone entirely — 'Recent Exports' is now fetched live via `GET /evidence/exports/history` (lines 142-174) with loading/error/empty states and a Retry button. Residual gaps (no export-scope filter, generic error handling on unsupported formats, history Download button bypassing the format-support gate) are tracked separately under EM-009/EM-032, which remain open.
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/ExportShareContent.jsx`
**Root Cause (original):** The "Generate Secure Link", "Send via Email", and "Portal Access" action cards rendered with no `onClick` handlers and no backend routes existed for any of these operations. The `staticRecentExports` fallback array contained hardcoded entries dated 2025-12-28 presented as real export history.
**Status:** FIXED — see fixEvidence.

title: Google Drive evidence import is completely non-functional — frontend calls connector-service routes that do not exist, and the BullMQ drive-upload worker is never started
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/services/integrationHubService.js:201-208` (`getDriveFiles`/`getDriveEvidence`/`uploadDriveFile`); `vibrantix-connector-service/src/routes/connector.routes.ts` (route registrations); `vibrantix-connector-service/src/services/ConnectorService.ts` (`getDriveFiles`/`getDriveEvidence`); `vibrantix-connector-service/src/index.ts` (worker wiring)
**Root Cause (original):** None of connector-service's registered route files implemented `GET /connectors/:id/drive/files`, `GET /connectors/:id/drive/evidence`, or `POST /connectors/:id/drive/upload`. The `drive-upload` BullMQ queue was instantiated at boot but `createDriveUploadWorker` was never imported or invoked — a complete functional absence at every layer.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-connector-service` (`feature/dev`, fast-forwarded 63ddaa5→4ca2ce7, merging commit `75a36b8` "QA testing fixes"). All three routes now exist in `connector.routes.ts` (permission-gated via `INTEGRATION_HUB_PERMISSIONS.VIEW`/`.MANAGE_EVIDENCE`, schema-validated), calling real `ConnectorService.getDriveFiles`/`getDriveEvidence` methods (not stubs) and a real queue-enqueue for upload. `index.ts:28,316` now imports and starts `createDriveUploadWorker(db, s3Service, redisConnection, fastify.log)` alongside the other two real workers. Traced the full route → service → worker chain and it holds together correctly end-to-end; no regression found.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-connector-service/src/routes/connector.routes.ts:818-1000+` (drive/files, drive/evidence, drive/upload routes, real service calls, not stubs) + `src/services/ConnectorService.ts:1638,1678` (`getDriveFiles`/`getDriveEvidence` implementations exist) + `src/index.ts:28,316` (`createDriveUploadWorker` now imported and started) — all confirmed present on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` for `vibrantix-connector-service` (HEAD now 4ca2ce7, includes commit 75a36b8 dated 2026-08-29 'QA testing fixes').

title: Every integration-evidence PDF export prints a hardcoded, non-computed ISO 27001/SOC 2/NIST control-mapping block regardless of the actual evidence — fabricated compliance data presented as genuine in a customer-facing audit artifact
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/IntegrationEvidenceDetailPage.jsx`
**Root Cause (original):** A static, hardcoded `COMPLIANCE_BADGES` array (unrelated to the evidence's actual provider/type/content) was printed identically on every exported PDF via `generateEvidencePDF`, presenting fabricated compliance data as a genuine, evidence-specific mapping.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`, fast-forwarded 9a5bac4f→d400be5a). `COMPLIANCE_BADGES` no longer exists anywhere in the file (confirmed zero matches). `generateEvidencePDF` (line 347) now takes a real `verdicts` parameter sourced from the same per-evidence control-verdict data already used on-screen, and prints "No control mappings recorded for this evidence." (line 418) when none exist for that specific item, rather than any static placeholder. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/IntegrationEvidenceDetailPage.jsx:347,418,1121` — `generateEvidencePDF(data, summary, mfaMetrics, eventCategories, versions, evidenceId, records, verdicts)` now sources real per-evidence `verdicts` and falls back to an honest empty-state string, confirmed on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` (client-panel HEAD now d400be5a).

title: Evidence requests can be marked 'fulfilled' without ever actually mapping a control - three disconnected manual steps stand between 'evidence exists' and 'control is covered'
description:
`EvidenceRequest` (`vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence-request/evidence-request.model.js`) only moves to `fulfilled` via the explicit `linkEvidence` action (`evidence-request.controller.js:311-357`), which the requester/assignee/admin must trigger by hand from `FulfillEvidenceRequestModal.jsx`. There is no code path anywhere in the upload controllers (`createEvidence`, `uploadAI`, `uploadAIBulk`, `confirmAI`) that looks up or auto-links an `EvidenceRequest` - confirmed by grep: zero references to `EvidenceRequest` anywhere under `modules/evidence/` or `core/`. Worse, the modal's own info box (`FulfillEvidenceRequestModal.jsx:338-340`) states plainly: 'This will attach the evidence to this request for review. The requester will review and accept it to attach to the requirement/check' - i.e., even marking the request `fulfilled` does NOT itself create the `EvidenceRequirementMapping`/`EvidenceUclMapping` needed for coverage; that is yet a third, separate manual action via the mapping UI.

Auditor-facing breakage: a requester can request evidence for Control X, someone can upload matching evidence and mark the request 'fulfilled,' and the control can still show 0% coverage because nobody separately performed the mapping step - three disconnected manual actions stand between 'evidence exists' and 'control is covered,' with no automation and no reconciliation check between them.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.3 documented information must be available; ISO/IEC 27007:2019 §6.3.2

title: Entire AI-metadata-validation resolve action (Accept AI Suggestions / Split to New) calls backend routes that do not exist — `POST /evidence-validation/workflow/:id/resolve` and `/resolve-with-assignee` 404 in production
description:
**Discovered while validating EM-010's 2026-08-29 'fix in progress' note.** `evidenceValidationService.js`'s `resolveWorkflow()` (line 85) and `resolveWorkflowWithAssignee()` (line 106) call `POST /evidence-validation/workflow/:workflowId/resolve` and `/resolve-with-assignee` respectively — the only two save actions in `EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx` (Accept AI Suggestions, Split to New). A repo-wide grep for `evidence-validation` across the entire `vibrantix-backend` codebase (re-run 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev`, commit 8641818) returns **zero matches** — no route, controller, or model exists anywhere under this path. Every call to either action in production returns a 404; the drawer's only two persistence actions are completely non-functional, independent of any frontend validation logic (EM-010's min-length/Textarea fix, now genuinely applied, gates an action that itself cannot succeed).
**Impact:** A reviewer can fill in a fully-valid resolution note, click Accept AI Suggestions or Split to New, and the request will 404 — the AI-upload metadata-validation review workflow this drawer exists for is entirely inert in the current codebase, with no error surfaced beyond a generic toast (see `handleAcceptAI`/`handleSplitFiles` catch blocks).
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
1. Decide where this logic should actually live — most likely as new endpoints on the existing evidence module (e.g. vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-validation.controller.js + routes), not a new top-level 'evidence-validation' module, to match this app's existing per-feature module convention.
2. Implement POST /evidence-validation/workflow/:workflowId/resolve and /resolve-with-assignee (or repoint the frontend service to wherever this logic is decided to live) — accepting filesResolutions, resolutionNotes (now sent by the frontend, see EM-010), and for the -with-assignee variant, assigneeId/note.
3. Persist resolutionNotes to a WorkflowEntry or equivalent audit-trail record so the ISO 19011 §6.4.9 justification EM-010 fixed on the frontend actually reaches durable storage.
4. Add an integration test exercising the full Accept-AI-Suggestions and Split-to-New flows end-to-end (drawer → service → backend → persisted record), so this gap cannot regress silently again.
```

title: Evidence version replacement does not force re-review; the coverage gate checks Evidence _id/status, not the version an approved mapping was actually created against
description:
`EvidenceVersionService.createVersionedUpdate` (`evidence-version.service.js:30-118`) bumps `version` but keeps the SAME `_id` for the new (latest) content (lines 96-98); the old content is snapshotted to a new `_id` with `isLatest:false`. `updateEvidence` (`evidence.controller.js:238-269`) does not force `status` back to a re-review state unless the caller's request body explicitly includes it - if a user replaces the file on an already-`closed` evidence record, the record's status silently stays `closed`. The real coverage gate, `recomputeCoverage`/`recomputeControlCoverage`, validates evidence purely by `{_id, status:'closed', isLatest:true}` (`client-compliance-sync.service.js:1805-1811,2634-2639`) - it never checks which `version` the original approved `EvidenceRequirementMapping`/`EvidenceUclMapping` (keyed by {evidenceId, version, requirementId/uclId}) was created against. Since the `_id` never changes across a version bump, a mapping approved for v1's content continues to satisfy coverage the instant v2's completely different file lands, with no re-review triggered.

Auditor-facing breakage: an auditor clicks 'evidence covering Control X,' opens the file, and is shown the CURRENT file - which may be an entirely different document than the one a reviewer actually assessed and approved - with the platform still reporting the control as 'closed'/satisfied.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.2(b) change history must be maintained; Clause 9.1
